title: DAL functions accept optional transactions
summary: Database access functions accept an optional transaction/client so services can compose multi-step writes atomically.
rationale: Services often need multi-step writes to commit or roll back as one unit.
Routes should stay HTTP-focused and not know persistence details.
One transaction-aware DAL pattern is cleaner than parallel transactional/non-transactional helpers.
required: DAL functions accept tx?: DatabaseClient as their final optional parameter.
DAL functions use const client = tx ?? db().
Services pass tx through composed write flows.
Routes call services for workflows instead of composing persistence directly.
replaced: DAL functions always calling db() internally.
Route handlers composing multi-step persistence directly.
agentPolicy: Use the required pattern for new code.
When touched code uses the replaced pattern, refactor the touched flow to the required pattern.
Do not add internal shims, aliases, compatibility wrappers, deprecated paths, or parallel APIs.
exceptions: Database migrations and persisted data.
Public API contracts already consumed outside the repo.
External integration formats.
examples: src/db/dal/company.ts shows the transaction-aware DAL shape.
src/api/routes/companies.ts shows a route calling a service instead of DAL.

title: Services compose DAL instead of direct DB clients
summary: Services own workflow composition but should use DAL modules for persistence details.
rationale: DAL modules keep table/query details in one layer.
Services stay focused on business sequencing and transactions.
required: Services call DAL functions for reads and writes.
Services pass tx through multi-step workflows.
Services do not import DB clients or table definitions for direct queries.
replaced: Services calling db() directly for ordinary persistence.
Services mixing workflow code with table/query construction.
agentPolicy: When touching service code that calls db(), move the query into a DAL function.
Do not add service-local query helpers as compatibility shims.
exceptions: Transaction orchestration may create or receive tx, but query construction still belongs in DAL.
Migrations and one-off maintenance scripts outside src/services.

title: Imports preserve local ownership boundaries
summary: Deep relative imports are treated as a boundary smell because they make layer ownership implicit.
rationale: Agents tend to copy nearby imports.
Deep relative paths make it hard to see whether a dependency direction is intentional.
required: Use local same-folder imports for private helpers.
Use package aliases or approved barrels for cross-layer imports.
Keep relative imports shallow.
replaced: Imports that climb multiple parent directories to reach another layer.
agentPolicy: When touching a deep relative import, replace it with the current approved import surface.
Do not create new barrels just to preserve stale import paths.
exceptions: Small colocated tests may use one parent traversal when the repo convention allows it.

title: Comments describe current intent
summary: Comments should explain current behavior, not preserve stale compatibility narratives.
rationale: Agents may treat comments as live instructions.
Legacy/deprecation/shim comments invite preserving old paths instead of cleaning touched code.
required: Use comments for non-obvious current intent.
Remove comments that justify legacy, deprecated, shim, or backward-compatibility paths when refactoring touched code.
replaced: Comments that instruct agents to keep stale compatibility code around.
agentPolicy: If a touched comment describes a legacy/shim/deprecated path, refactor the touched flow and remove the stale comment.
Do not add compatibility comments for internal code.
exceptions: External public API migrations and persisted data migrations may document compatibility constraints explicitly.

title: Use const objects instead of native TypeScript enums
summary: Enum-like values use JavaScript const objects plus a derived union type instead of native TypeScript enums.
rationale: Const objects are plain JavaScript and avoid TypeScript enum runtime semantics.
The pattern keeps value casing and type naming visible to agents and reviewers.
required: Use PascalCase names for enum-like const objects.
Use PascalCase keys.
Use string literal values.
Export a matching derived union type with the same name.
replaced: Native enum and const enum declarations.
agentPolicy: Replace touched native enums with const object plus derived union type.
Only apply automatic rewrites when member names and string values can be preserved exactly.
exceptions: External generated TypeScript definitions outside source ownership.
examples: export const CompanyStatus = { Active: "active" } as const;
export type CompanyStatus = (typeof CompanyStatus)[keyof typeof CompanyStatus];

title: Schemas define contracts at package boundaries
summary: Validation schemas and DTO contracts live at boundaries; internals use typed domain objects.
rationale: Boundary schemas stabilize request/response contracts.
Database table definitions are persistence details and should not leak into public DTO modules.
required: Route inputs are validated at the API boundary.
DTO schemas are exported from the contract layer.
Database schemas stay in the database layer.
Services translate between contract DTOs and persistence records.
replaced: Inline route-only schemas duplicated across handlers.
Importing database table definitions into public contract modules.
agentPolicy: Move duplicated boundary schemas to the contract layer when touching that flow.
Keep database schema details out of public DTO modules.
Refactor touched imports to the current boundary direction.
exceptions: One-off test fixtures.
Small local schemas for private route query parsing.

title: Tests scale with blast radius
summary: Narrow changes get focused unit tests; shared behavior and cross-layer workflows need broader tests.
rationale: Tests should catch regressions at the same boundary where the risk was introduced.
required: Unit tests cover local branching and data mapping.
Integration tests cover database/service contracts.
Route tests cover validation and response shape.
Use the project test script instead of a tool-specific shortcut.
replaced: Only testing the happy path after changing shared behavior.
Testing third-party libraries instead of local integration behavior.
agentPolicy: Add or update tests near the changed behavior.
When refactoring touched stale patterns, update tests in the same pass.
Do not preserve old test helpers if all touched call sites can move cleanly.
exceptions: Pure docs-only edits.
Mechanical formatting-only changes.

title: Python modules use package imports instead of sys.path mutation
summary: Python code should use normal package/module configuration rather than mutating sys.path at runtime.
rationale: Runtime path mutation hides dependency boundaries.
Package imports are easier for tests, agents, and tooling to reason about.
required: Use package imports.
Configure module paths in the runner, test config, or packaging metadata.
Keep imports stable and visible at file top level.
replaced: Calling sys.path.append(...) or sys.path.insert(...) inside source modules.
agentPolicy: When touching Python code with sys.path mutation, replace it with package imports.
Do not add import-path shims inside source files.
exceptions: Standalone one-off scripts outside source packages.

title: Folders use approved responsibility names
summary: Folders should communicate ownership and layer responsibility instead of becoming dumping grounds.
rationale: Agents copy folder names they see.
Ambiguous folders make ownership and import direction harder to infer.
required: Use existing layer folders before creating new top-level folders.
Use the `*.service.ts` or `*.service.tsx` suffix for service implementation files.
Choose folder names by responsibility, not short-lived intent.
Add a decision before introducing a new broad folder category.
replaced: misc, helpers, common, temp, new, draft as source folder names.
Unsuffixed service implementation files such as src/services/company.ts.
agentPolicy: Do not create dumping-ground folders.
If touched files live in a dumping-ground folder, move the touched flow to the current structure.
exceptions: Third-party generated output outside source ownership.

title: Impact surfaces describe sensitive downstream effects
summary: Sensitive files and domain resources are linked through impact surfaces so agents can see downstream effects before changing them.
rationale: Import graphs miss domain dependencies such as data, events, jobs, permissions, and external contracts.
Agents need explicit risk context before changing sensitive surfaces.
required: Enforced impact surfaces link docs and decisions.
Sensitive changes satisfy the surface change policy.
Agent-discovered impact notes remain proposed until reviewed.
agentPolicy: When touching persistent data, events, permissions, jobs, contracts, or high-risk domain logic, check existing impact surfaces.
Update or propose impact notes only when grounded in concrete evidence.
Do not enforce guessed downstream relationships.
exceptions: Exploratory proposed impact notes may exist without enforcement.

title: Framework packages depend inward only
summary: OpenCanon framework package imports follow the package responsibility graph.
rationale: Core contracts should stay reusable without pulling in CLI, daemon, UI, or engine code.
Package-level direction keeps runtime, validation, and UI concerns independently testable.
Agents can safely add files when the allowed dependency direction is explicit.
required: Core does not import other framework packages.
Validators and engine may import core only.
Daemon may import core, engine, and validators.
CLI may import core and daemon.
UI source does not import framework runtime packages directly.
replaced: Cross-package imports based on convenience rather than package responsibility.
UI code importing runtime package internals instead of using daemon APIs or local DTOs.
agentPolicy: When adding a framework package import, check the package responsibility graph first.
Move shared contracts into core instead of importing upward.
Keep UI communication through daemon APIs or explicit local DTOs.
exceptions: Tests may import package internals when testing that package directly.
Release and rehearsal scripts may import source modules as build orchestration.

title: Secrets and environment config stay out of source literals
summary: Source code should not contain live-looking secrets or environment-specific configuration literals.
rationale: Committed secrets are difficult to revoke reliably after publication.
Hardcoded URLs, hosts, and ports make deployment environments harder to change.
Agents may copy literal values unless config ownership is explicit.
required: Use secret managers or environment variables for credentials.
Use named config objects or project settings for environment-specific values.
Keep allowed placeholders clearly synthetic.
replaced: API keys, tokens, passwords, client secrets, or private keys committed in source.
Deployment-specific URLs, hosts, and ports embedded directly in runtime code.
agentPolicy: When adding code that needs a credential, add a config lookup and document the expected variable name instead of committing a value.
When adding an environment-specific URL, host, or port, prefer a named config surface.
Keep test fixtures and examples synthetic.
exceptions: Loopback development defaults may be allowlisted.
Tests, fixtures, and docs may use clearly synthetic placeholder values.
Public release URLs may be allowlisted when they identify published artifacts rather than environment secrets.
